dedupe_keys.name: opendhn data meshed district heating network benchmark verbier

description: OpenDHN data is a benchmark for simulating meshed district heating networks, built from anonymised monitoring data. Version 1.0.1 was published on Zenodo in March 2024 by Roberto Boghetti and Jérôme Henri Kämpf, with the method described in their CISBAT 2023 paper. It contains average sensor measurements from the meshed district heating network of Verbier, an alpine resort in Switzerland, powered by two heating plants and serving 150 substations. The measurements are meant to be compared with simulation results, and code for reproducing the paper is in a separate benchmark repository. Coverage is Verbier, Switzerland. The data are one small zipped archive, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: data are anonymised averages, and one network is covered. Simulation uses are validating thermal-hydraulic simulation of meshed heat networks and testing digital twin and state estimation methods. Related records: data-verbier-meshed-district-heating-citysim-dataset gives full simulation inputs for the same network.
